nodes.label: API Wire Boundary Normalization
nodes.rationale: Normalize frontend/backend data-shape mismatches only at the active API wire boundary (dashboard, dev tools, lib/server, backend controllers/services), using inline fixes rather than new mapper modules or a shared/api-dto package, to limit blast radius. DB schema and legacy frontend routes (frontend/legacy/, app/memo/) were deliberately left out of scope. Target conventions: scholarId on wire, camelCase response fields, {data: T} envelope, WAHF spelling with /wahf/ route aliases alongside legacy /whaf/.

nodes.author: miguelventura1123@gmail.com
nodes.norm_label: fix signup email confirm token hash

nodes.label: Supabase Email-Confirmation Template Fix
nodes.rationale: Root cause: /auth/confirm expects token_hash+type (verifyOtp SSR pattern) but the default Supabase 'Confirm signup' template uses {{ .ConfirmationURL }}, which redirects with a PKCE code or hash tokens the route never reads. Senior-dev minimal-refactor stance: editing the one Supabase email template is preferable to a dual-path code refactor; a code-only exchangeCodeForSession fallback was rejected as tactical debt because of cross-device PKCE limitations.

nodes.author: miguelventura1123@gmail.com

nodes.label: Dev Test Profiles + Containerized CI Pipeline
nodes.author: miguelventura1123@gmail.com
nodes.norm_label: dev test profiles + containerized ci pipeline

nodes.label: Acting-Mode Mutation Denylist (rejectWritesWhenActing)
nodes.rationale: Developer 'acting as' a test profile needs read access on POST-shaped read endpoints (e.g. recent-submissions) but must not perform true mutations (sync, profile create, memo refresh). Fixed a dashboard 403 by allowing read-via-POST endpoints through while keeping a denylist that blocks true mutating routes during acting mode, rather than blocking all POST traffic outright.

nodes.label: Doc Review + Security Audit + Remove hasEnvVars
nodes.author: miguelventura1123@gmail.com
nodes.norm_label: doc review + security audit + remove hasenvvars

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Session Check
nodes.rationale: hasEnvVars previously let middleware skip auth session checks when Supabase env vars appeared unset, an unintended bypass surfaced by a security audit. Removed so middleware always enforces the session check (fail-closed) regardless of env var presence.

nodes.label: Campus Week Calendar Preferred Over /api/auth/semester
nodes.rationale: /api/auth/semester and /api/auth/active-semester should be used sparingly, in favor of the shared, server-owned campus week calendar as the source of truth for the current time frame. Legitimate exception: use the auth semester endpoints when the server-owned campus calendar does not make sense, e.g. when looking at historical data, or when the current collection year has not started yet.

nodes.label: TypeDoc API doc exclusion for default-only Express routers
nodes.rationale: backend/src/routes modules default-export an Express Router with no named exports, so TypeDoc renders them as empty pages; excluding routes from TypeDoc and pointing the Routes handbook to REST API + controller handler docs avoids the empty-page problem. Index generation also skips default-only modules and docs/reference/api is wiped before each TypeDoc run to avoid stale pages.
nodes.norm_label: typedoc api doc exclusion for default-only express routers

nodes.label: Smoke test endpoint/CORS fix and CI teardown removal
nodes.rationale: smoke-test.sh probed a nonexistent /api/memo route (should be /api/memo/weekly) causing a false FAIL, and CORS checks failed because the Origin header did not match Docker Compose's localhost:3000; fixed by probing the correct route and adding SMOKE_ORIGIN (default localhost:3000). CI docker compose tear-down was dropped from the smoke-test job on the assumption teardown works.
nodes.norm_label: smoke test endpoint/cors fix and ci teardown removal

nodes.label: Supabase-vs-codebase schema drift remediation plan
nodes.rationale: Recommended phased remediation: inventory/baseline drift, make git migrations the source of truth, generate Database types for the backend client, introduce shared API DTOs to eliminate the FE/BE/DB triple mirror, and add CI drift detection. Logged as an architectural alert via scripts/alert.sh.

nodes.label: Deployment topology documentation (Railway/Vercel/Docker Compose)
nodes.rationale: Cross-referenced open architectural alerts against dev-ops gaps and researched Supabase free-tier branching limits, then documented runtime topology (Railway split vs Vercel experimentalServices), Docker Compose CI/parity, CI/docs workflows, env wiring, and smoke validation in docs/dev/deployment/README.md as the canonical deployment handbook hub.

nodes.label: Nixpacks auto-build vs explicit Dockerfile trade-off
nodes.rationale: Nixpacks auto-detects language/stack and builds without config, while Docker requires an explicit Dockerfile; this monorepo uses root Dockerfiles because shared/ sits outside the backend/frontend package roots, so Railway's Nixpacks alone cannot see the shared workspace dependency and Docker is required for correct builds.
nodes.norm_label: nixpacks auto-build vs explicit dockerfile trade-off

nodes.label: New-developer onboarding guided path
nodes.rationale: Built docs/dev/onboarding (index, Day 0 setup, golden-path first PR, roles/personas, campus weeks, auth/RLS runbook, ask/don't-touch) using dual senior-dev/junior-dev roleplay to shape content, linking the PR template and mailto contacts for the three writers (Miguel, Ben, Moosay) so new contributors have a single guided entry point.

nodes.label: Day 0 auth redirect caused by backend being down
nodes.rationale: When the backend is not running or misconfigured, /api/auth/me fails and the frontend redirects the user back to login/dashboard, which looks like an auth bug to a new developer but is actually a Day 0 environment failure; documented as a known failure row in day-0-setup.md and mirrored in the auth/RLS runbook.
nodes.norm_label: day 0 auth redirect caused by backend being down

nodes.label: Developer handbook docs depth/trim policy
nodes.rationale: The handbook (docs/dev) had grown too many near-duplicate leaf READMEs; decided references (docs/reference) are CI-generated to accurately reflect inline code comments, while docs/dev is a human-authored handbook, so leaf READMEs were collapsed into standards hubs, unique Standards salvaged upward, empty dirs deleted, and mkdocs/nav + index-generation tooling updated to a hub-only, KEEP-set model.

nodes.label: next-themes dark mode with centralized semantic color tokens
nodes.rationale: Wired next-themes ThemeProvider/ThemeToggle/themed Toaster and extended globals.css with success/warning/info and domain semantic tokens so components no longer hardcode hex/palette colors. Traffic previously broke theming mid-animation, so its transition-all usage was replaced with semantic tokens and no blanket transitions; added theme-safety helpers, Vitest coverage, and scripts/check-theme-safety.mjs wired into CI to prevent regressions.
nodes.norm_label: next-themes dark mode with centralized semantic color tokens

nodes.label: Soft status badge muted-foreground token pairing
nodes.rationale: Soft status chips (e.g. '3 hrs left') looked off in dark mode because they used raw palette colors; fixed by adding success/warning/info muted-foreground tokens and Badge variants (success|warning|info) so soft chips always pair a muted background with a matching muted-foreground ink, extended into the theme-safety antipattern scan run in CI.
nodes.norm_label: soft status badge muted-foreground token pairing

nodes.label: Team-leader-only page redirect using effective auth profile
nodes.rationale: Sidebar gating already hid TL-only nav correctly, but memo/personal/traffic(logged-in) pages did not redirect scholars or acting-as-scholar personas who navigated directly by URL; fixed by aligning page-level redirects with the effective /api/auth/me profile (canAccessWeeklyMemo + getCurrentProfile) so gating is consistent between sidebar visibility and direct navigation.
nodes.norm_label: team-leader-only page redirect using effective auth profile

nodes.label: /traffic as a public, ungated foot-traffic kiosk
nodes.rationale: /traffic records foot traffic and must be usable by anyone without signing in, so all role/auth redirects were removed from its layout; safety is instead enforced at the write boundary via a Zod-validated recordTrafficEntry server action (forced traffic_type, no client-supplied created_at) plus optional Supabase RLS restricting inserts to anon/authenticated. Analytics views remain auth-gated on /api/traffic and /dev/traffic.
nodes.norm_label: /traffic as a public, ungated foot-traffic kiosk

nodes.label: GitHub-only ticket workflow (Issue Forms + architecture alerts)
nodes.rationale: Moved ticket/alert tracking onto native GitHub Issues: added Bug/Feature/Chore/Architecture-alert Issue Forms, an ensure-issue-labels script, an issue-triage Action that auto-applies needs-triage, and retargeted alert.sh/resolve-alert.sh to create/close-if-open GitHub Issues instead of markdown alert files, with a migration script for the 7 legacy alert files (blocked on gh auth at time of logging).
nodes.norm_label: github-only ticket workflow (issue forms + architecture alerts)

nodes.label: Backend-Only Supabase Access Pattern
nodes.rationale: For this stack, domain access is backend services querying Supabase Postgres tables/RPCs directly; no Supabase Edge Functions are invoked from the app, keeping data access centralized in the backend service layer.

nodes.label: CODEOWNERS / Branching Review Policy
nodes.rationale: Junior Developers may only branch off develop, make changes, and PR into develop with Senior Developer approval, never touching main. Senior Developers may write directly to develop and main, but merging develop into main requires 2 Senior Developer approvals. The user dislikes that seniors can write directly to main but accepts the tradeoff deliberately to minimize time-to-hotfix when a small but important bug slips through.
